scenes.headline: How a geometry kernel keeps a solid exact
scenes.sub: An industrial kernel goes open source, with solids stored in the scene graph
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Fillet! An industrial geometry kernel just went open source. Here is how a kernel keeps a solid exact.

scenes.text: A solid is exact surfaces plus topology: which trimmed piece of which surface is kept, and which pieces touch, kept consistent while operations cut and stitch.
scenes.say: A mesh is just triangles. A kernel's solid is exact surfaces plus topology: which trimmed pieces are kept, and which ones touch.

steps.say: A model splits space into regions, solid and void, each bounded by a shell of faces.
A face is a piece of an exact surface: a plane, a cylinder, or a spline patch.
Loops of edges say which part is kept. Outer loops run one way, holes the other.
Every edge carries an exact curve and knows each face it bounds.
Every time a face, loop or edge bounds something, that incidence is its own use. A face has two, one per side.
So one edge can bound three or four faces mid boolean, which simpler structures cannot hold.

scenes.title: How a boolean runs
scenes.say: A boolean runs in four careful phases.

items.say: Find every place the two solids meet, in scratch space.
Merge pieces within tolerance, and stop if anything failed.
Only then imprint the cuts into the real solids.
Classify each face as inside or outside, and keep what the operation wants.

scenes.say: And the kernel is no toy: nearly a million lines of code.

scenes.text: An open kernel means anyone can read, fix and embed the hard parts: trimming, tolerances and booleans.
scenes.mark: read, fix and embed the hard parts
scenes.say: Within a day, outside developers had fixed real bugs. Open means anyone can read, fix and embed the hard parts.

recap: Solids stored as flat arrays in the scene
scenes.say: Exact surfaces, explicit neighbours, and solids in the scene graph. See you next time!
